fullPassage: Imagine you are pedalling your bicycle on a level road. You stop pedalling: no force is now acting to move you forward. What happens? You gradually slow down. How could you slow down more suddenly, in a shorter distance? By putting the brakes on. Because the brakes change your movement, making you slow down more suddenly, they must be exerting a force on the bicycle and you, as they grip and rub on the wheel-rims. This is the force called friction, which tends to slow down moving things by acting in the direction opposite to movement, that is backwards. Even without the brakes on, there are other friction forces acting on you and your bicycle, which also slow you down. One of these is friction in the wheels rubbing on the axles. Another is air resistance, which you can feel, pushing you backwards as you and the bicycle move forwards. When you apply these ideas to something around you, like a cart, you can see what could be generating friction: mainly the axles rubbing on the body as they rotate.

questions.passage:
(A) After years of training, she reached a very high <u>level</u> of skill.
(B) Imagine you are pedalling your bicycle on a <u>level</u> road.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 level의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: level: (A) 기술의 높은 수준 / (B) 평평한 도로
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 평평한: (A)는 기술의 '수준'을 뜻하므로 부적절
✅ ② (A) 수준 — (B) 평평한: (A)는 'a very high level of skill'에서 수준, (B)는 'a level road'에서 평평한이라는 두 의미를 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ③ (B) 쌓아 올리다: (B)는 동사가 아닌 형용사 '평평한'
❌ ④ (A) 건물의 층: (A)는 '층'이 아닌 '수준'
det.tip: level: ① (명사) 수준/정도 ② (형용사) 평평한 ③ (동사) 평평하게 하다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the force that resists motion between two surfaces that are touching"

det.korean: friction=마찰(력): 맞닿은 두 표면 사이의 운동에 저항하는 힘
det.analysis:
❌ ① distance: '거리'는 두 지점 사이의 간격으로 힘이 아님
❌ ② balance: '균형'은 힘의 평형 상태이지 저항력이 아님
❌ ③ movement: '움직임'은 운동 자체이지 저항하는 힘이 아님
✅ ④ friction: '마찰(력)'은 맞닿은 두 표면 사이의 운동에 저항하는 힘으로 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: friction = 마찰력. resists motion between two surfaces가 핵심

questions.passage: Because the brakes change your movement, __________ (make) you slow down more suddenly, they must be exerting a force on the bicycle and you. This is the force called friction, which tends to slow down moving things by acting in the direction opposite to movement, that is backwards.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 분사구문: 주절과 동시에 일어나는 동작을 현재분사(-ing)로 표현
det.analysis: 주절 'the brakes change your movement'에 동시 상황을 더하는 분사구문. 접속사+주어 없이 동사가 올 때 현재분사(V-ing)를 쓴다. make → making
det.tip: 분사구문 = V-ing (동시동작). making you slow down = 당신을 느리게 하면서

questions.passage: This is the force __________ (call) friction, which tends to slow down moving things by acting in the direction opposite to movement. Even without the brakes on, there are other friction forces acting on you and your bicycle, which also slow you down.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 과거분사의 형용사적 수식: the force (which is) called friction
det.analysis: 명사 the force를 뒤에서 수식하는 과거분사. 'the force (that is) called friction(마찰이라 불리는 힘)' 구조로, 수동 의미이므로 과거분사 called가 적절. call → called
det.tip: 명사 + 과거분사(p.p.) = ~되는/~된 (수동 수식). the force called friction

questions.passage: Imagine you are pedalling your bicycle on a level road. You stop pedalling: no force is now acting to move you forward. What happens? You gradually slow down. How could you slow down more suddenly, in a shorter distance? By __________. Because the brakes change your movement, making you slow down more suddenly, they must be exerting a force on the bicycle and you, as they grip and rub on the wheel-rims. This is the force called friction, which tends to slow down moving things by acting in the direction opposite to movement, that is backwards. Even without the brakes on, there are other friction forces acting on you and your bicycle, which also slow you down. One of these is friction in the wheels rubbing on the axles. Another is air resistance, which you can feel, pushing you backwards as you and the bicycle move forwards. When you apply these ideas to something around you, like a cart, you can see what could be generating friction: mainly the axles rubbing on the body as they rotate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: putting the brakes on=브레이크를 작동시키는 것 — 더 갑자기 멈추는 방법
det.analysis:
✅ ① putting the brakes on: 원문 일치. 더 짧은 거리에서 더 갑자기 멈추는 방법은 브레이크를 작동시키는 것이다 ←정답
❌ ② speeding up the wheels: '바퀴 속도를 높이는 것'은 멈추는 것과 반대
❌ ③ removing the front tire: '앞 타이어 제거'는 본문에 근거 없음
❌ ④ leaning to one side: '한쪽으로 기우는 것'은 제동과 무관
det.tip: How could you slow down more suddenly? By putting the brakes on.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: acting in the direction opposite to movement=움직임의 반대 방향으로 작용하는 것 — 마찰이 물체를 느리게 하는 방식
det.analysis:
❌ ① increasing the speed of rotation: 회전 속도를 높이는 것은 느려지게 하는 마찰과 반대
❌ ② reducing the weight of the moving object: 무게 감소는 본문에 근거 없음
✅ ③ acting in the direction opposite to movement: 원문 일치. 마찰력은 움직임의 반대 방향(즉 뒤쪽)으로 작용하여 움직이는 물체를 느리게 한다 ←정답
❌ ④ changing the shape of the wheel-rims: 바퀴 테 모양 변경은 본문에 근거 없음
